facts.value: You can apply with either the ASU application or the Common Application — ASU does not prefer one over the other — but you should submit only one.
The application typically takes less than 30 minutes to complete.
Apply as early as possible — the earlier you apply, the sooner you’ll receive an admission decision.
No. ACT/SAT scores are not required for admission to ASU or to be considered for an ASU merit-based scholarship, but they are encouraged.
Barrett requires a separate application. You may apply to Barrett after you submit your ASU admission application but you do not need to wait for an admission decision from ASU.
Use My ASU, the ASU admissions portal to check your application status.
If your status shows missing transcripts or materials, follow the instructions in your portal and submit the required items as soon as possible.
When applying, avoid using a school email address, as you may lose access to it after graduation.
